problems.quote: “All A are B” + “Some B are C” → “Some A are C” (definite)
problems.problem: The middle term B is undistributed in both premises (predicate of A is undistributed, subject of I is undistributed), so no valid conclusion follows; “Some A are C” is not definite.
problems.correction: “All A are B” + “Some B are C” yields no definite conclusion.
problems.verifierReason: Middle term B undistributed in both premises; no valid conclusion follows.

problems.quote: A complementary pair in syllogism consists of two conclusions that cannot both be false at the same time.
problems.problem: This definition describes sub-contraries, not the complementary (contradictory) pairs used in either-or questions; the contrary pair (A vs E) can both be false, so it does not fit the definition.
problems.correction: A complementary pair in syllogism consists of two contradictory conclusions (A vs O or E vs I) that cannot both be true and cannot both be false.
problems.verifierReason: Complementary pairs are contradictories (A/O, E/I), not sub-contraries; correction is accurate.

problems.quote: the middle term C is distributed in the universal
problems.problem: In “All A are C”, the predicate C is undistributed; only the subject of a universal affirmative is distributed. Thus the middle term is not distributed and no conclusion follows.
problems.correction: the middle term C is undistributed in “All A are C”, so no definite conclusion follows.
problems.verifierReason: In 'All A are C', predicate C is undistributed; middle term undistributed yields no conclusion.

problems.quote: “No A are D” cannot be derived because the middle term C is not distributed in “All C are D”
problems.problem: In “All C are D”, the subject C is distributed; the middle term is distributed, so “No A are D” can be derived (valid Cesare mood).
problems.correction: “No A are D” can be derived because the middle term C is distributed in “All C are D”.
problems.verifierReason: In 'All C are D', subject C is distributed; Cesare mood validly yields 'No A are D'.

problems.quote: The valid conclusion is “Some A are not C” (O)
problems.problem: The premises are two negatives (E and O), which commit the fallacy of exclusive premises; no conclusion follows.
problems.correction: No valid conclusion follows because two negative premises yield no conclusion.
problems.verifierReason: Two negative premises (E and O) commit fallacy of exclusive premises; no conclusion follows.

problems.quote: Hanahan and Weinberg’s seminal reviews (2000, 2011) defined eight core hallmarks of cancer
problems.problem: The 2000 review defined six hallmarks; eight were defined in the 2011 review.
problems.correction: Hanahan and Weinberg’s 2011 review defined eight core hallmarks of cancer (expanding from six in 2000)
problems.verifierReason: 2000 review defined 6 hallmarks; 2011 review expanded to 8. Quote incorrectly attributes 8 to both.

problems.problem: Taxanes are microtubule-stabilising agents, not destabilising.
problems.verifierReason: Taxanes stabilize microtubules; vinca alkaloids destabilize. 'Microtubule-targeting agents' is the correct umbrella term.

problems.quote: if Q K it proceeds in reverse
problems.problem: Missing comparison operator; the reaction proceeds in reverse when Q > K, not when Q < K.
problems.correction: if Q > K it proceeds in reverse
problems.verifierReason: Original quote missing operator; reaction proceeds reverse only when Q > K. Correction is chemically accurate.

problems.quote: when the relation itself changes at each step, e.g., 'Square : Cube :: Circle : Sphere :: Triangle : ?'
problems.problem: The example provided does not illustrate a changing relation; the text explicitly states the relation repeats ('the second step repeats the same dimensional lift'), making it a constant relation example.
problems.correction: when the relation remains constant across steps, e.g., 'Square : Cube :: Circle : Sphere :: Triangle : ?'

problems.quote: (initial bearing of object in fixed frame) − (observer's heading change) = bearing in observer's frame
problems.problem: The formula omits the observer's initial heading. Correct relation: bearing in observer frame = (bearing of object in fixed frame) − (observer's current heading) = (initial bearing in observer frame) − (heading change).
problems.correction: (initial bearing in observer frame) − (observer's heading change) = bearing in observer's frame
problems.verifierReason: Original formula uses fixed-frame bearing instead of observer-frame bearing; correction matches standard relative bearing kinematics.
